$comment: VAPP-108: the rewrite gap list. Every app screen of packages/view-catalog/views.json (the exponential-ui-catalog group excepted: those ARE the catalog) classified by what the core catalog needs before the screen could be written as an Exponential UI surface: `expressible` = today's catalog + the app extension (IconDisc, LiveDot) draw it; `macro` = one or more missing layout macros (named) would make it one surface without Box + style; `extension` = an app-specific component the app extension must add (a painter per platform, never the core catalog); `native` = a new core NATIVE (a renderer-level control: an editor, a terminal, a diff, a tree with drag) the catalog does not have. `with` names what is missing. gaps.test.ts keeps this list in lockstep with views.json. VAPP-126: `landed` = the candidate macros now in the catalog (Page, Toolbar, FieldGroup, FormActions, SplitView, StatTile); the 13 screens that waited only on them are `expressible`, settings-team-agent `native` (its markdown editor is what is left).

renderers.$comment: Which gaps concern which web renderer now that there are three (FEED-128: @exponential_app/eui-solid; FEED-130: @exponential_app/eui-element, the <exponential-surface> element on the Solid painter). A `macro` expands in the shared reducer before any renderer sees it: no renderer work. An `extension` component is painted by the app extension, which exists for React only (defineReactExtension): a Solid twin (defineSolidExtension) is needed before an extension-class screen runs on Solid, and the element inherits it (defineElementExtension wraps the same painter). A `native` is a renderer-level control every renderer must paint: Solid included, so each native candidate is one more Solid painter, which the element then gets for free.
